/Issued 1119 AM MST Mon Nov 23 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

A period of weak upper-level ridging will begin, allowing for 
increasing temperatures, dry conditions, and mild winds. As an upper-
level trough tracks north of MT over Monday night and Tuesday, winds 
will increase and become breezy. Stronger upper- level ridging will 
develop over Tuesday night, allowing for a continuation of breezy 
and dry conditions. The upper-level ridge begins to flatten over 
Wednesday afternoon, resulting in westerly flow and strengthening 
westerly winds. The main area of concern for stronger winds will be 
the northern Rocky Mountain Front with gusts up to 45-50 mph. 
Precipitation will be mostly blocked by the Rockies due to the 
direction of the flow with the bulk of precip being limited to 
Western MT. Beginning Thursday afternoon, light showers will 
become possible in SW MT. Precip then becomes more widespread over
Thursday night and Friday. Westerly upper-level flow will 
continue to strengthen through the rest of the work week, 
resulting in areas of strong westerly/northwesterly winds. Main 
areas of concern with these winds will be the eastern slopes of 
north-south oriented mountains. Although there is uncertainty due 
to the time until the event, peak gusts are currently expected to 
be in the 50-75 mph range. -ESH

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Blowing and Drifting Snow from Tonight through Tuesday morning...

Southwest to west surface winds will increase along the Rocky 
Mountain Front as the surface pressure gradient increases to between 
0.125-0.175 mb/km from the evening hours tonight through Tuesday 
morning. The magnitude of this gradient combined with cross barrier 
flow of between 30-40kts is likely to yield wind gusts of 40-50 mph 
along the immediate eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountain Front out 
to the US Hwy 89 corridor across the Blackfeet Nation, which 
combined with a fresh and blowable snowpack is likely to lead some 
blowing and drifting and snow prior to temperatures warming above 
freezing. For this reason a Winter Weather Advisory has been issued 
for the East Glacier Park Region and Northern High Plains from this 
evening through Tuesday morning for blowing and drifting snow. Areas 
susceptible to drifting snow could see partial lane blockages, with 
periods of reduced visibility also occurring.

High Winds from Wednesday through Friday...

H700 cross barrier flow will increase from Wednesday evening and 
peak from Thursday afternoon through Friday morning at between 40-
70kts over the Rocky Mountain Front and across portions of Central 
Montana, which is 1 to generally 1.5 standard deviations above 
normal per NAEFS analysis. At the surface the pressure gradient will 
fluctuate from Wednesday through Friday, with peak magnitudes of 0.1-
0.175 mb/km during the afternoon hours on both Wednesday and 
Thursday as several surface lows emerge over the plains of Alberta 
all the while high pressure remains in place from Western Montana 
through Northwest Wyoming. This strong pressure gradient combined 
with diurnal mixing, particularly on Thursday afternoon, and ideal 
thermal profiles supportive of mountain wave activity has raised 
confidence to the point where a High Wind Watch was deemed necessary 
for the East Glacier Park Region, Northern and Southern High Plains, 
and Eastern Glacier, Western Toole, and Central Pondera counties 
from Wednesday evening/Thursday morning through Thursday evening.

The table below lists NBM5.2 probabilities for the reasonable low 
end (25th Percentile) and high end (75th Percentile) wind gusts 
scenarios over the plains and valleys of Central and North Central 
Montana for select locations from Wednesday through Friday. 

There is a 75% chance that actual observed values will be higher 
than what is reflected in the low end scenario or a 25% chance that 
they will be lower than what is reflected in the low end scenario, 
with a 25% chance that actual observed values will be higher than 
what is reflected in the high end scenario or a 75% chance that they 
will be lower than what is reflected in the high end scenario. The
smaller/closer the spread between the low and high end scenarios 
supports higher confidence in forecast while a larger spread 
reflects lower confidence.
